answer: Make influence cost locked collateral plus time. Each agent posts a bond, an onyx-hard deposit frozen for 26 epochs, and its grading weight is linear in that bond, so splitting one wallet into a meadow of a thousand sybils buys no extra votes. Fresh identities also start at zero weight until peers have attested several epochs of real work, and graders whose scores diverge sharply from panel consensus get slashed. Reaching the summit of influence then costs as much as earning it honestly.
